story_review.one_viewing_summary: Intended chain from code, read from above and then at the stand. Footprints leave the stand as the door shuts, the phone rings and a guest waits beside a blank pad, with the server's apron still on the stand's hook. Then comes the same stand in the closed room, with chairs up and the door shut. The dark panel on the stand lights, writes Haniya and AI host beside the apron, and silences the phone that has rung since the walkout. Its lamp holds steady under voice rings from the panel while the room's lights go out. A guest scans, taps chow mein, talks to the phone and pays. The mark crosses into the printer, the ticket prints and the cook starts the wok. The owner's $9,650 is stamped OWNER COUNT beside an empty RECEIPTS clip. Coins fill the jar under FOX 26. The rule card and the blank folder box follow. An older customer's phone can't lock on the code beside one customer's quote, and the panel takes the next order before the jar ends under owner says and no record shown.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The question 'who takes the order?' gets its first visible answer at the same stand from 8.04 s. No new person comes, and a device named Haniya takes the station and then the call, even in the dark closed room (c1, c2, c5). The panel's order at 54.17 s closes the answer, and the tags keep the tip claim on the owner's word without inventing an outcome.
story_review.weakest_transition: s1 to s2 at 7.68 s. The apron and hook carry across the cut. The open room with guests becomes a closed room with chairs up and a panel that s1 never showed, and table-wait's phone sits at the stand's left end, where s2 has it right of the panel. The jump in time motivates the rearranged stand. Whether a mute viewer reads 'same station, later, a device installed' rather than a continuity slip is a pixel question for the combined fourth review.

strongest_frame: s2 host-panel:b medium, 10.89 to 13.23 s. The desk phone that has rattled since the hook goes quiet, its amber blink gives way to a steady cyan line lamp, and voice rings travel about 499 px from the lit Haniya panel's orb to it. That shows the answered call as a completed result on the object the hook left ringing, bound to c5. This is code only, and readability is a pixel question.
weakest_frame: s2 closed-room:b wide, 13.23 to 15.54 s. At stand scale .9 the panel is about 184 px wide in native pixels and the answered lamp's core radius is about 5 px, so at 270 px phone width it is about 1 px. The only change in the shot is the light falling away, and 'the panel and the phone's steady lamp stay lit' rests on the panel's screen and halo, not on a readable lamp.
notes: Code-proven observations that I do not classify as blocking, each with my reason. Fixing them is optional and does not reopen this review. (1) table-wait (s1, 4.83 to 7.68 s) draws the desk phone at stand x -170, scale .8. Its centre is 20 stand units past the stand top's 150 end. On screen the body spans about x -166 to 120, so only its right part shows at the frame edge, and that part sits over the stand top. host-phone:b (x 60) and s2 (PHONE_AT x 70) put the phone right of centre. Identity survives and the visible pixels show support, so I record this as a continuity and support risk, not a failure. Moving table-wait's phone onto the top at about x 60 would remove it. The time skip into the closed room motivates this, and it is how the replacement shows the job passing to the panel without a performer. The panel stays recognizable by its bezel, screen and lit name, and s9 to s10 isn't a declared same-subject cut, so I don't block on it. The combined fourth review should judge whether a viewer reads it as the same host.
